Process_Text.original: PAAs synthesized from PMDA and ODA was designated as PAAs1 after neutralization. PAAs1 was dissolved in deionized water at 70 °C to obtain 1 wt% sizing solution. Bare-CF samples were immersed in PAAs1 solution for 20 min, then dried and subsequently heated to 300 °C for 60 min to induce imidization. The resulting modified fibers were designated as PI1-CF. CF/PEI composites were fabricated using a vacuum hot-pressing technique at 330 °C under a pressure of 4 MPa.
Process_Text.simplified: PAA synthesis (PMDA+ODA in DMAc, neutralize with TEA) → dissolve in water (1 wt%, 70 °C) → immerse CF 20 min → imidize 300 °C/60 min → vacuum hot-press with PEI at 330 °C/4 MPa

Stage4_Composite_Fabrication.Layup: 9 layers PEI film / 8 layers CF fabric

Structure_Text.original: PI1 exhibits no discernible glass transition below 380 °C (Tg > 380 °C), which can be attributed to its highly rigid molecular backbone formed by the condensation of PMDA and ODA. After PI coating, the groove structures became visibly shallower, indicating the formation of a polymeric film layer on the fiber surface.
Structure_Text.simplified: PI1: highly rigid backbone, Tg > 380 °C; PI1 coating fills CF surface grooves

Sizing_Layer_Tg.Note: Tg > 380 °C; not observed below 380 °C, so exact value unknown

FTIR_Imide_Characteristic.Note: confirms complete imidization; applies to all three PIs

Properties.Note: slightly lower ILSS than Bare-CF/PEI (58.9 MPa) despite improved flexural strength; attributed to high Tg of PI1 limiting interdiffusion with matrix
